The aPTT assay is SATURATED by PS content at 2 mg/mL in vitro, so it has no dynamic range left to separate a toxic sequence from a safe one. effect_direction is deliberately NOT_REPORTED, never no_change. so that no S57 row silently carries S57b content.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT NUMERIC. Only 5 of the 17 sources yielded any number at all. Every value in this file is either quoted
verbatim from running text or marked NOT_REPORTED. NO NUMBER WAS EVER READ OFF A FIGURE. Sources S53, S54, S55 and S59 keep
their coagulation values exclusively in plotted panels (S53: Figs 1A-1D, 4A-4F, 6E, S3B-S3C; S54: Fig 7A; S55: Figs 1C-1F,
3A-3D; S59: Fig 4), and every row from them carries readout_is_qualitative = true with readout_value NOT_REPORTED. The three
triage 'granularity conflicts' (S53, S54, S55) are therefore resolved conservatively as qualitative, as instructed.

CONTRADICTIONS AND ERRORS FOUND, LISTED SO A REVIEWER CAN CHECK THEM.
1. S58 DOI IS WRONG ON THE TRIAGE SHEET. The file's own <article-id pub-id-type="doi"> reads 10.1089/nat.2015.0533; the
   triage sheet recorded 10.1089/nat.2015.0537. The file's value is used. Journal/volume/page from the same element:
   Nucleic Acid Ther 2015;25(3):130-.
2. S47 IS NOT 'ABSOLUTE SECONDS'. The triage sheet called the 18/21/23 s figures absolute post-infusion PTT values. The
   sentence actually says 'partial thromboplastin time prolongation values ... were 18, 21 and 23 s', i.e. INCREMENTS over
   baseline. No baseline PTT is printed. The rows are labelled accordingly; treating them as absolute PTT would be wrong.
   The abstract also does not call them medians, so no central-tendency statistic is asserted.
3. S39 DOSE LISTS DISAGREE WITH THEMSELVES. The abstract gives dose groups as '4, 8, 12, and 40 mg/kg/wk' and then reports
   results for '20 or 40 mg/kg/wk'. 20 is not in the first list. Both strings are recorded exactly as printed; the paywalled
   full text is needed to resolve it. Do not build a dose-response from this abstract.
4. S54 SPECIES CONTRADICTION. The Results text says clotting times were evaluated 'in mouse plasma'; the Figure 7A legend
   says 'analysed in human plasma'; the Methods say 'Mouse or Human citrated plasma samples'. species is set to human,
   following the figure legend, which is the panel that carries the n values. Flagged on all eight S54 rows.
5. S63 INTERNAL TENSION. 'bruising in all dose groups' vs '2 mg/kg ISIS 2302 produced no remarkable alterations'. Both are
   recorded. Note 'all dose groups' as printed would literally include the 0 mg/kg control.
6. S59 FIGURE CROSS-REFERENCE IS AMBIGUOUS. Section 3.9 (coagulation) cites '(Figure 4)', but the Figure 4 caption in the
   same file reads 'Effects of NVP-13 on hematological parameters (A-Q)' and never names PT or APTT panels. The coagulation
   panels are presumably among A-Q; this could not be confirmed from the XML.
7. S65 INTERNAL TENSION. The abstract reports 'dose-related increases in activated partial thromboplastin time' and also
   'No adverse events or other laboratory abnormalities were related to treatment' - the authors evidently did not classify
   the aPTT change as an abnormality. Recorded as printed, not reconciled.

THE ASSAY-LIMITATION FLAG (S55), STATED PLAINLY BECAUSE IT IS EASY TO MIS-ENCODE. S55 measured aPTT and found it could not
separate a toxic from a nontoxic PS-tcDNA, 'since aPTT is already prolonged and saturated by PS-ASO in vitro'. That is a
METHOD LIMITATION, not a safety finding and not a null. The S55 aPTT row carries effect_direction NOT_REPORTED, deliberately
never no_change. Any pipeline that reads an in vitro aPTT null at high PS-ASO concentration as evidence of safety is misusing
the assay. Note the direction of the surprise: everywhere else in this bundle aPTT is the SENSITIVE assay (S48, S56, S57) and
PT the insensitive one; in S55, at 2 mg/mL in vitro, that ordering inverts because aPTT has saturated.

THE CENTRAL SCIENTIFIC TENSION IN THIS BUNDLE. S48 and S57, from two independent sponsors, state that the coagulation effect
is SEQUENCE-INDEPENDENT and PS-BACKBONE-DEPENDENT. S55 is a documented counterexample: identical chemistry, identical PS
content, significantly different PT, reversed by a single A->G wobble substitution, and accompanied by real in vivo bleeding.
S53 adds a second qualification: PS POSITION matters, not only PS count, and HDOs with MORE PS modifications gave SHORTER
aPTT than their parent ASOs. 'Sequence-independent' must therefore be encoded as a claim attributable to S48/S57, never as a
dataset-wide law. Nothing in this file asserts a resolution.

DOUBLE-COUNTING HAZARDS. ISIS 2302 is the subject of S47, S48, S49, S56, S63 and S65. These are six papers but they are not
six independent observations of the class effect; S47 and S65 in particular are the same compound in humans (one numeric, one
qualitative) and the triage sheet already warns against counting them separately. S48 and S49 are the same laboratory on the
same mechanism. Any meta-analysis must cluster by compound and by laboratory.

DELIBERATE SCHEMA DEVIATIONS, ALL FLAGGED IN THE ROWS THEMSELVES.
- readout_unit 'nM' is used for the S49 binding and inhibition constants (K_D 11.5 / 4.8 / 92 nM, K_I 88 nM) and 'nmol/L' for
  the added factor Xa in S48. The schema's unit enum contains no molar member, and mapping a nanomolar constant onto ng/mL or
  %_of_control would have been a fabrication. Enum fidelity was traded for numerical honesty.
- The S39 '33% increase in APTT' row uses readout_unit '%_of_control' because the enum has no percent-change member. THE
  NUMBER 33 IS A PERCENT INCREASE, NOT 33% OF CONTROL. Same trap on the '80%' FXI reduction row. Both are called out in row
  notes. By contrast the S48 'approximately 35% of control' tenase row and the S67 'below 5% of baseline' row genuinely ARE
  percent-of-control.
- study_type 'ex_vivo_human_plasma' is the only ex vivo enum member, but S56 spiked MONKEY whole blood. species=monkey and
  matrix=whole_blood are set so the mismatch is visible rather than hidden.

EFFECT_DIRECTION SEMANTICS. Several rows use 'decrease' to mean MITIGATION of an oligonucleotide-induced prolongation rather
than a value below normal - all the S53 DabO rows, the S57 protamine reversal row, the S56 infusion-duration row. Every such
row says so in effect_vs_control. Two S48 add-back rows use 'no_change' to mean 'the added factor FAILED to correct the
prolonged PTT', which is a negative correction result, not a normal PTT. Read effect_vs_control, not effect_direction alone.
S49's K_D row is the sharpest trap: the value RISES from 4.8 to 11.5 nM while the AFFINITY FALLS.

ABSENCE ROWS. Measured nulls (effect_direction = no_change): S39 PT, bleeding challenge and platelets; S48 modified Russell
viper venom time; S49 FIXa-phospholipid FX activation, FVIII-phospholipid affinity, FVIIIa half-life; S54 all four PO-backbone
rows; S55 H51(+67)W PT (mouse and human) and platelet activation; S56 chromogenic FXa/FXIa/thrombin and the heparin-mechanism
comparison; S58 MGN1703 aPTT; S59 PT and APTT; S63 2 mg/kg clotting times and the platelet/RBC counts. Distinguished from

NOT_REPORTED; S64's subcutaneous row is an INFERENCE from the exclusive phrase 'by intravenous dosing only' and is labelled
as weaker evidence than a quoted null; S55's aPTT row is a METHOD LIMITATION. These four categories must not be merged.

PLATELET ROWS. Four were kept, each because the source ties the platelet readout to a coagulation-cascade result: S39 and S63

refused_rows:
1. S53 PLATELET COUNT (Figure 6F). The source measured platelet count in mice 6 h after 20 mg/kg Chol-HDO and reports that a
   Dab12 complex 'partially ameliorated thrombocytopenia'. REFUSED because the source's own Discussion attributes
   thrombocytopenia to a DIFFERENT mechanism from the coagulation finding - interaction of PS-ASOs with platelet GPVI and PF4
   - rather than to the intrinsic-tenase/aPTT axis. It is co-reported with aPTT as a 'class-related toxicity' but is not tied
   to a coagulation-cascade readout, so it belongs to the separate thrombocytopenia endpoint, not here. Contrast S39 and S63,
   where the platelet result IS used to reason about the coagulation finding and was therefore kept.

2. S53 CEREBRAL INFARCTION / FOCAL BRAIN NECROSIS (abstract; Figures 7C-7E). The abstract says DabO conjugation 'effectively
   prevented cerebral infarction, a condition frequently observed in mice intravenously injected with high-dose Chol-HDO', and
   the Results describe focal necrosis in cerebral cortex, hippocampus, inferior colliculus and cerebellum at 50 mg/kg.
   REFUSED as a thrombotic_outcome row because the endpoint definition requires a thrombotic outcome ATTRIBUTABLE TO A
   COAGULATION DEFECT, and this source makes no such attribution anywhere - it offers no coagulation mechanism for the brain
   lesions, and the terms 'cerebral infarction' (abstract) and 'focal necrosis' (Results) are not reconciled by the authors.
   Recording it would have imported an unstated causal claim. Flagged here because it is genuinely interesting and a reviewer
   with the full figures may decide otherwise.

   (20-mer ASOs and cRNAs with distinct PS placement patterns) and each has its own aPTT. REFUSED as per-variant rows because
